title: Sophie Tucker and Al Jolson visit; Twinkle Davis and the Panama girls
summary: Downtown stars like Tucker and Jolson came up to hear them; Twinkle Davis had legs, Goldie Crosby, Mamie Carter and Nellie Carr could sing or dance.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And perform. See? And there's where all the people from downtown would come up, like Sophie Tucker

and Al Jolson. And oh, what is that thing that Al Jolson came up there and asked me to show him how to sing? Something about a little black boy. It'll come to me later, but I'll tell you later. He -- I didn't teach him how, but I showed him how I sang it, you know.

And Sophie Tucker. Now, I'm getting ahead of myself. No, I'm going to stay there. The Panama. That's the Panama. We made a lot of money at the Panama. Twinkle Davis had the most beautiful limbs you ever saw. She reminded me so much of Marlene Dietrich, you know, now that I know what it's all about. Twinkle, she couldn't do anything but walk out on the floor, and that was all she had to do. She didn't have to do anything else. She was an attractive girl. She was good looking. But that's all she had, was her legs. She tried to dance, but she was as bad a dancer as I was a story teller.
So anyhow, Goldie Crosby could sing a little. Mamie Carter, she could sing a little, and then Nellie Carr used to do a dance and run and split, do the splits.
